They Can't Get to You Here

Your safety and anonymity are protected by multiple layers of legal, technical and professional safeguards. From emergency response to encryption, every measure has been designed to keep you secure.

Emergency Response Image

Emergency Response First

If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 999 immediately. Our platform supports ongoing investigations and accountability, but emergency services respond to immediate threats to life and safety.

Our designated safeguarding leads are trained to recognise urgent situations and can escalate directly to appropriate authorities within hours, not days. However, if there's immediate risk, don't wait - contact emergency services first.

Emergency: 999 Childline: 0800 1111

If You Are Under 16

Before you send anything, try to speak with a trusted adult like a parent, teacher, or family member first. If that's not possible, organisations like Childline, the NSPCC, or local churches can provide support.

When young people submit reports, our system automatically flags them for priority review so they are examined first, quickly before anyone else. We work with established children's charities to ensure proper support is available and can arrange for trusted adults to help with the process if needed.

Childline Support NSPCC Help
Under-16 Protection Image
Alternative Support Image

When You Can't Trust the Police

Police involvement in cover-ups makes many victims reluctant to report through official channels. This site provides an alternative route to accountability whilst connecting you with independent charities and support services.

Victim Support, Rape Crisis centres, and specialist abuse charities operate independently from police and local authorities. They can provide confidential support, practical help, and advocacy services without requiring you to make formal reports if you're not ready.

Victim Support Rape Crisis

Complete Anonymity Available

You can submit reports without providing any identifying information whatsoever. We don't require names, addresses, email accounts, or phone numbers. Anonymous submissions receive the same careful attention as identified reports.

Even if you provide contact details, we will never share your identity without your explicit written consent. The only exception is immediate safeguarding emergencies where someone's life may be at risk - and even then, we'll tell you what we had to disclose and why.

Your Choice, Your Control

Security Software Image

Military-Grade Security Software

Our platform runs on GlobalLeaks - the same software trusted by the International Criminal Court, major European governments, and international human rights organisations. This isn't a social media contact form.

Every submission is encrypted end-to-end, meaning even if someone intercepts your report, they see only meaningless scrambled text. The platform undergoes regular penetration testing and security audits by independent experts, with all reports publicly available.

Technical Details GlobalLeaks.org

Vetted Security Engineers

Our engineers are professionals with extensive experience in handling sensitive government and legal systems, not freelance web developers.

Additionally, technical staff cannot access the content of encrypted submissions - they can maintain the servers but cannot read your reports. Only qualified legal professionals with appropriate clearance can decrypt and review submission content.

DBS Checked Staff

US Constitutional Protection

Our servers operate under United States jurisdiction, which provides First Amendment protection for journalistic and public interest activities. This means corrupt UK officials cannot easily pressure us to hand over information or shut down operations.

US courts require much higher standards of evidence and legal justification before ordering disclosure of journalistic sources or whistleblower information. This constitutional protection has historically shielded reporters investigating government corruption and institutional abuse.

Read the First Amendment 1A Whistleblower Protection

End-to-End Encryption & Secure Storage

Every submission is encrypted using AES-256 encryption (the same standard used by governments for top-secret documents) from the moment you click submit. Your report travels through multiple layers of SSL/TLS protection with an SSLabs A+ security rating.

Data is stored on hardened servers in secure US cloud facilities with 24/7 monitoring, biometric access controls, and multiple backup systems. Even if someone physically broke into our provider's data centre, they would find only encrypted files that are useless without decryption keys held separately.

AES-256 Encryption SSLabs A+ Rated
Encryption & Storage Image
Legal Professional Access Image

Barrister-Only Access & AI Protection

Only qualified barristers bound by professional privilege can access submission content. Before human review, reports undergo private anonymous AI scanning to identify urgent safeguarding concerns and protect case workers from traumatic content exposure.

This AI screening helps identify patterns across thousands of reports whilst preserving anonymity and enables faster response to emergency situations. The AI systems are isolated from external networks and operate under the same encryption and security standards as the main platform. They have no internet access.

Legal Privilege Protected
Anonymous AI Screening

Do Not Submit Testimony to Amateur Websites

Many political groups in the UK, mostly well-intended, have created basic forms on their websites for victims to report crimes. These are often email addresses, web "survey" forms you might find on Instagram, or software "plugin" forms with no security at all. None of the "teams" behind these efforts have taken any efforts to provide for victim safeguarding, data security, or training in processing crime reports which may need emergency escalation. If in doubt, contact a legal professional before you send private information to people you don't know on the internet.
